overview.problemStatement: quota-ledger 0.1 ships a Postgres backend. Services that already run Redis but not Postgres cannot share quota state without adding a database, so they fall back to a per-process counter that resets on deploy and lets two pods spend the same last unit.
overview.proposedSolution: Add an additive `redis` feature to quota-ledger that implements the existing QuotaStore trait over a caller-supplied Redis connection. The atomic claim is a server-side Lua script so concurrent reservations cannot exceed a budget, and every operation keeps the 0.1 contract: tenant-scoped keys, commit-once, release, idempotency conflict, and a typed QuotaExceeded carrying the reset instant.
overview.targetAudience: Rust services that already operate Redis and need shared provider quota without a relational database.
assumptions: The 0.1 QuotaStore contract is stable enough to implement against; no trait change is expected.
The caller supplies a connected redis client; the crate reads no environment variable or connection string.
The redis crate version must resolve on Rust 1.87; otherwise the feature stops rather than raising the MSRV.
Redis 7 or later, so EVALSHA and TIME are available.
No live Redis is available in CI, so concurrency proof needs an opt-in harness recorded as a risk.

userStories.title: Share quota state through Redis
userStories.want: the ledger to live in Redis
userStories.benefit: quota survives restarts and is consistent across pods without adding Postgres

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a redis feature build and a caller-supplied connection, when reserve is called with remaining capacity, then it records a hold and returns a reservation with an identifier, using only Redis keys scoped by tenant, provider, metric, and window.
Given concurrent reserve calls against one limited budget, when all complete, then the total committed never exceeds the limit because the claim is one server-side script.
Given an open reservation, when commit is called twice, then the hold is consumed exactly once and a repeated commit is rejected or idempotent.
Given a caller idempotency key already used with a different payload, when reserve is called again, then it fails with the typed idempotency conflict and takes no second hold.
Given no capacity and HardStop, when reserve is called, then it returns a typed QuotaExceeded carrying the reset instant and creates no reservation.
Given a key with reservations, when usage is read, then it reports limit, consumed, held, and the next reset instant computed from the configured window.
Given the crate built with default features, when it compiles, then no Redis type is present; and with all features on Rust 1.87 it compiles with forbid(unsafe_code) and deny(missing_docs).
Given a Redis failure or a malformed payload, when an operation runs, then it returns a typed QuotaError and the error never renders the connection string or a credential.

functionalRequirements.text: A `redis` feature MUST add a QuotaStore implementation backed by a caller-supplied connection and MUST be absent when the feature is off.
The reserve claim MUST be a single server-side script so concurrent claims cannot exceed the limit.
commit MUST consume a hold exactly once; release MUST return held units.
Idempotency keys MUST be honored per tenant, provider, metric, and window, and a conflicting payload MUST return a typed conflict.
Budget and reservation keys MUST embed the tenant, so no operation can read or spend another tenant's quota (CON-512).
Windows MUST support daily, monthly, and rolling resets computed from the window, not from host midnight.
The crate MUST NOT read environment variables, connection strings, or credential files (CON-519).
Errors MUST NOT render a connection string, a password, or a Redis URI (CON-214).

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Every Redis key MUST be namespaced by tenant and MUST NOT collide across providers or metrics (CON-512).
The script and every command MUST pass caller values as arguments, never as interpolated command text (CON-516).
Caller-supplied windows, metrics, and unit counts MUST be validated and bounded before reaching Redis (CON-515).
The crate MUST compile on Rust 1.87 with all features (CON-102).
Every public item MUST carry rustdoc and every module MUST state its scope and non-goals (CON-202, CON-203).

edgeCases.description: Two pods reserve the final unit simultaneously
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: exactly one script call succeeds; the other returns QuotaExceeded.

edgeCases.description: Redis restarts between reserve and commit
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: a missing reservation returns a typed not-found error, never a synthetic success.
it settles against the window it was created in; the reset instant is derived from the key, not the clock.
the crate compiles and links no Redis client, and sqlx stays the only optional backend.
typed QuotaError::Backend, redacted, with no partial hold.

dependencies.name: redis
dependencies.notes: Async, TLS-capable, behind the redis feature; must resolve on Rust 1.87.

dependencies.name: tokio
dependencies.notes: Dev-dependency only, for the opt-in Redis harness.

risks.description: No Redis in CI, so the concurrency proof needs an opt-in harness.
risks.mitigation: AC-002 asserts the script's atomicity through a Redis-backed test when a server is available, and the gap is documented in the review rather than implied to be covered.

risks.description: Lua scripts are easy to get subtly wrong around expiry and settlement.
risks.mitigation: The script is the review's focus and gets its own failure-path tests for missing, expired, and already-settled reservations.

risks.description: A redis release that needs Rust 1.88 or later blocks the feature.
risks.mitigation: Pin a compatible release, or stop and amend CON-102; never raise the MSRV silently.
